nodes.title: Start here
widgets_values:
# Build a timeline Premiere can import

**No Premiere plugin needed**, and this one runs exactly as shipped -- it uses ComfyUI's own `example.png`, so just press **Run**.

Two one-second clips get made (one plain, one colour-inverted) and handed to **Save Premiere Timeline**, which lays them end to end on V1 and writes a folder.

**What you get:** `output/premiere_timelines/Bridge Demo/`, holding `Bridge Demo.xml`, `Bridge Demo.edl` and a `media/` folder with the clips in it. Click **Open folder** on the Save node to go straight there.

**In Premiere:** `File > Import` the **.xml**. The sequence turns up with its media already linked -- no relinking, no dragging clips into place.

The colour inversion is only there so you can tell the two clips apart at a glance and know the order came out right.

nodes.title: Swap this out for your own work
widgets_values:
## This half is a stand-in

**Load Image > Repeat Image Batch > Create Video** is the cheapest possible way to make a video clip: one still, held for 24 frames, at 24fps. One second.

Replace it with whatever you actually generate. An image workflow feeding Create Video, or a video model's output going straight into the Save node -- anything that produces a **VIDEO** will do. Nothing else in this file has to change.

Want a different picture? Swap `example.png` on the Load Image node for any image already in your ComfyUI `input` folder, or upload one.

Want longer clips? Raise **Repeat Image Batch**'s amount. 24 frames per second of footage.

# One absolute media path per line, added after the video_N inputs.
# Blank lines and # comments are ignored.

nodes.title: Every setting on the Save node
widgets_values:
## Save Premiere Timeline

**video_1, video_2, ...** -- connect the last empty socket and a fresh one appears. Wire in as many clips as you like; they land on V1 in socket order.

**sequence_name** names both the folder and the sequence you'll see in Premiere.

**fps** is the sequence's frame rate. Keep it matching what you fed Create Video, or the clips play at the wrong speed.

**media** -- this only affects the **paths** entries below; wired `video_N` clips are always written into `media/` either way. *Link in place* points the edit at your listed files where they already sit. *Collect into folder* copies them into `media/` next to the .xml first, which is what you want if the folder is going to somebody else.

**paths** -- anything you type in here gets added after the wired clips, one absolute file path per line. Handy for dropping in footage that never went through ComfyUI. Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored, which is why the box already has two comment lines in it.

**write_edl** is on, so you also get a plain `.edl` that almost any editor will open.
**write_otio** stays off -- it needs an extra Python package installed first.

**output_dir** left empty means ComfyUI's own output folder. Type a path to write somewhere else.
